about: General as a value cell with no number format of its own shows it (ADR-0060; the seventeenth Windows run, item 16): at most eleven characters besides a minus sign, which is '-' in every culture, as ExSheet's General at twelve characters or wider (ADR-0047, SH-20). Transcribed from the C# engine's PivotGeneralTests.

cases.name: ADR-0060, item 16: the values Excel's PivotTable showed in General (expivot-cells.md e05a, e05b, e08, e16)
ADR-0060 (SH-20's rule): rounding that carries an integer part into a twelfth digit goes scientific
ADR-0060 (SH-20's rule): a minus sign is not one of the eleven characters, a reading, as ExSheet's: the run asked no negative number
ADR-0060: General writes the culture's decimal separator: en-US
ADR-0060: General writes the culture's decimal separator: de-DE
ADR-0060: General writes the culture's decimal separator: ja-JP
ADR-0060: General writes the culture's decimal separator: fr-FR
ADR-0060 (by generalisation: no run read Excel under these cultures): the minus sign is '-' in sv-SE, as ExSheet's General writes it, never the culture's U+2212
ADR-0060 (by generalisation: no run read Excel under these cultures): the minus sign is '-' in fi-FI, as ExSheet's General writes it, never the culture's U+2212
ADR-0060 (by generalisation: no run read Excel under these cultures): the minus sign is '-' in nb-NO, as ExSheet's General writes it, never the culture's U+2212
ADR-0060: zero, and a negative zero, are 0
ADR-0060 ("Money stays exact"): an exact decimal is shown from its own digits, under the same rule
ADR-0060: the closer form is judged from the fifteen digits both forms are built from, never from a decimal's further ones; these showed 1E-01 and 1E+00
ADR-0060 (the edge, as stated): a double is judged against its own value, so where a decimal's fifteen digits tie between the two forms, its double can choose the other
